To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the yield stress in tension of compact bone is determined primarily by Young's modulus and the post-yield stress is determined primarily by the mineral content of the bone.
the post-yield behaviour of compact bone in tension depends more on the mineral (calcium, phosphate, carbonate) content of bone than on the Young's modulus.

yield strain varies much less than the strain after the onset of plastic deformation, and that the onset of plastic behaviour is determined by Young's modulus but the subsequent plastic behaviour is determined primarily by mineral content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between mineral content, mechanical properties, and post-yield behaviour of compact bone.
the mechanical behaviour of the mineral component of bone.
the relationships between mineral content, strain, stress and work in compact bone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the yield stress of compact bone in tension is determined by Young's modulus, and post-yield events by mineral (calcite) content.
the mineral content of bone, and the mineral content alone, is a major determinant of post-yield behaviour.
yield in tension is determined by the strain and post-yield behaviour of bone is determined by the mineral content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
yield strain is the most important determinant of yield stress in bone.
mineral content determines the post-yield behaviour of bone and that this is a function of the amount of collagen in the matrix.
the mineral content of bone, as a percentage of dry weight, is a better predictor of post-yield properties of bone than of pre-yield properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mineral content of compact bone is a good predictor of its post-yield behaviour.

post-yield events are more dependent on mineral content, and therefore on the collagen-mineral matrix interactions, than on Young's modulus and yield strain, which are more dependent on the collagen matrix.
mineral content is more important for predicting the post-yield behaviour of compact bone than is Young's modulus.
